reasoning: The deepseek model correctly reviewed all repository files and found the PKGBUILD to be a standard, safe AUR packaging script. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was solely due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400) when attempting to review .SRCINFO and .gitignore. Per the rules, tool errors carry no verdict signal. The actual package contents pose no injection risk.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from a tool failure in the qwen model (API HTTP 400 errors for .SRCINFO and .gitignore), not a genuine security disagreement. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO and .gitignore due to LLM API HTTP 400 errors, causing an invalid inconclusive overall verdict.
learnings: The audit tool should not mark the entire package as inconclusive if API errors occur on non-executable metadata files (.SRCINFO, .gitignore) while the critical executable file (PKGBUILD) is successfully audited and found safe.
Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient LLM API errors to prevent unnecessary inconclusive verdicts.
